# Rootwall

> Provider conduct, on record. A membership for the providers that connect to your systems. Rules agreed in advance with every provider that connects to your systems, a signed account of how each one keeps them, and a record of every time one is broken.

Website: https://rootwall.ai
Contact: info@rootwall.ai
Company: ROOTWALL.AI LTD, registered in England and Wales, company number 12578817. Based in London, working with organisations anywhere.

## The problem

Your providers come in through doors you opened for them. An IT supplier on your VPN, a payroll firm on your API, a support company with a remote tool. You vetted them once. When one of them breaks your rules you can block it, and that is all. Nothing was agreed in advance, nothing is recorded, and nothing follows it to the next renewal.

## How it works

Both sides check. Rootwall compares and keeps the record. Nobody hands over logs. Each side checks the agreed rules on its own logs and sends Rootwall a short signed statement.

1. Agree the rules. Rootwall writes the rules for each provider's access with you, and the provider accepts them before it connects.
2. Both sides check. A checker reads your logs where they sit. The provider can run one on its side too. Each sends a signed statement, never the logs.
3. Compare and record. Rootwall compares the two accounts. Every broken rule is a strike on that provider's record, ready for your next contract renewal.

## Who it's for

One record, read from both ends of the connection.

- For the head of security: Your providers answer for their own doors. Your attention goes back to the doors nobody answers for. The doors you opened for providers come with rules they agreed to and a record you both can see.
- For third-party risk: Evidence for the renewal, not a questionnaire. A provider's conduct over the whole contract, rule by rule, with both sides' signed account. Bring it to the table when the contract comes up.
- For providers: Your clients trust you with the keys. A clean record shows them you deserve it. Send your own signed statements and your account stands beside theirs.

## What it is not

It adds a record. It replaces nothing you run.

- Not a security operations centre. Your security team keeps its own detection, untouched. Rootwall checks agreed rules and nothing else.
- Not a firewall or gateway. Rootwall never sits in your traffic. It sets the rules and keeps the record.
- Not identity. Your providers already prove who they are. Rootwall records how they behave once they are in.

## The company

Defenders cannot keep watching every door alone. The companies that hold the keys should answer for the doors they use. Rootwall is a London company built by people from the defending side of security.

## Common questions

What is Rootwall?
Rootwall is a membership for the providers that connect to your systems: rules agreed in advance, and a signed record of how each one keeps them.

Who counts as a provider?
Any company you let into your systems: IT support, outsourced operations, software vendors, payroll firms and similar.

Is it a firewall or a gateway?
No. Rootwall never sits in your traffic. Your firewalls and gateways stay exactly as they are.

Is it a security operations centre?
No. Your security team, in-house or outsourced, keeps its own detection, untouched.

Is it an identity product?
No. Your providers already prove who they are. Rootwall records how they behave once they are in.

Do you take our logs?
No. Each side checks its own logs and sends Rootwall only a short signed statement of whether the rules were kept.

What happens when a provider breaks a rule?
It gets a strike on its record. The record is yours to bring to the next contract renewal.

Does the provider take part?
Yes. The rules are agreed with the provider before it connects. It can also send its own signed statements, so its account stands beside yours.

Where are you based?
In London, working with organisations anywhere.

How do we start?
Write one line to info@rootwall.ai. You will talk to the founder.
